Consult Summary:
- 40-year-old woman with 3-week history of left-sided hearing loss and facial numbness, referred for urgent in-person assessment.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Reduced hearing in left ear and numbness along left jawline/around left ear for approximately 3 weeks.
- Associated symptoms: Occasional ringing in left ear, sometimes associated with dizziness. Numbness present most of the time. No ear discharge, ear pain, fever, difficulty swallowing, speech problems, vision issues, or generalized weakness/numbness.
- Pertinent negatives: No ear discharge, pain, or fever; no other neurological deficits.
- Past medical history: Nasal polyps (uses nasal spray as needed, name not recalled), prior history of labyrinthitis (not ongoing); no other chronic illnesses noted.
- Medications: Nasal spray (name, dose/route/frequency not documented); Rennie as needed for unspecified symptoms; no other regular medications.
- Allergies: Latex.
- Family history: Brother with neurofibromatosis; otherwise non-contributory.
- Social history: Works as a jockey, symptoms affecting ability to train; lives with partner; no pets.
- Preventive care: Not mentioned.

Examination:
- (No examination findings documented in transcript.)

Impression:
- Working diagnosis: Bell’s Palsy (left-sided), to be confirmed on physical examination; urgent neurological assessment recommended to rule out other causes.

Plan:
- Advise urgent, in-person evaluation and neurological/ear examination today in clinic.
- Administrative support to arrange same-day face-to-face appointment in Central London.
- Reassurance provided that diagnosis is unlikely to be life-threatening.
- Plan to further counsel/explain Bell’s Palsy if confirmed.
- Patient instructed to contact support team to confirm appointment.

Quality checks:

●	Missing clinically expected elements: No documentation of full medication reconciliation, immunization/preventive care history, baseline vital signs, or detailed neurological/eardrum exam (pending in-person appointment). No detailed allergy history beyond latex. No documentation of occupation-related risks or recent trauma.
●	Internal conflicts: Contradictory living situation reported (“live alone” and “live with my partner”)—conflict noted.
●	Transcript quality: Clear overall; some noise and incomplete sentences but clinically relevant details were obtainable.
